instruction: In the opened movies spreadsheet, create a new sheet called 'classic_movies' with all movies released before 1960. Keep the same headers and sort the results by release year from earliest to latest.

command: import pyautogui; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); import time; time.sleep(1)

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent created an 'unseen_movies' sheet but copied ALL seen_movies data instead of finding unseen IMDB Top 30 movies. Never visited IMDB website. Attempted to sort data in the new sheet.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can create new sheets in LibreOffice Calc, copy data between sheets, use sort dialog, navigate between sheet tabs, right-click context menus
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed because it never visited IMDB to get the Top 30 list. Instead, it copied all existing seen_movies to unseen_movies sheet. The cross-application comparison (Chrome + Calc) was too complex.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to filtering movies by year (before 1960). No external website needed. Sort by release year ascending is a different sort target than the original, testing the model's ability to configure sorting correctly.
metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a new sheet with pre-1960 movies sorted by release year ascending. Evaluator checks: sheet exists with correct name, headers match, row count is 30, and data is sorted by release year ascending.

scoring_breakdown.headers_match: 0.25 - Headers match original (title, release year, ratings, description)
scoring_breakdown.sort_order: 0.25 - Sorted by release year from earliest to latest

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the 'classic_movies' sheet from the xlsx file, returning sheet_name, headers, rows (as dicts keyed by header name), and row_count - all needed by the metric.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': accesses expected.get('expected_sheet_name') etc. directly from the rules dict without incorrect nesting.
Postconfig properly activates the window and saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring fresh file state.
All four verification aspects are checked: sheet name (0.25), headers match (0.25), row count (0.25), sort order (0.25) with reasonable partial credit logic.

COVERAGE GAP: The evaluator does NOT verify that the rows actually contain movies released before 1960. It only checks row count=30 and ascending sort by 'release year'. An agent could copy any 30 rows sorted by year and score full marks without correctly filtering by year<1960.
The combination of exact count (30) + correct sort order provides a reasonable but imperfect proxy for correct filtering, since the dataset presumably has exactly 30 pre-1960 movies.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add a check in the metric to verify that all rows have 'release year' < 1960, e.g.: if all(float(str(r.get(sort_key, 9999))) < 1960 for r in rows): score += bonus or integrate into existing sort check.
Consider adding the year threshold (1960) to the expected rules as 'max_year' and checking it in the metric to ensure the filtering condition is actually verified.
